section_summary: This section comprises U.S. Office of Naval Intelligence (ONI) bi-weekly intelligence summaries from the Naval Attaché in Tokyo and related State Department Division of Far Eastern Affairs memoranda from March through September 1933. The documents detail Japan's domestic political maneuvering under the Saito Cabinet, the aftermath of the May 15 incident, military operations and economic development in Manchukuo and North China, and growing friction over trade and naval parity with Great Britain and the United States. Additionally, the materials track Soviet-Japanese border and fisheries tensions, Chinese Eastern Railway purchase negotiations, military budget disputes, domestic social distress, and nationalist and anti-espionage agitation.

subfiles.about: Reports on Japanese legislative developments, the League of Nations withdrawal crisis, military operations in Jehol, Soviet relations, and domestic economic and social unrest.
subfiles.summary: Covers the Diet's consideration of the national budget, major legislative proposals, and the appointment of Kurahei Yuasa as Minister of the Imperial Household. Analyzes widespread public and military anticipation of Japan's departure from the League of Nations and preparations for the Jehol expedition in North China. Reviews Soviet refusal to enter a non-aggression pact, reactions to U.S. Pacific fleet movements, domestic naval training, urban vacancies in Tokyo, and widespread police roundups of political suspects.
subfiles.title: Tokyo Naval Attaché Bi-Weekly Intelligence Summary (Early 1933, Copy 1)

subfiles.about: Reviews the Tokyo Naval Attaché's May 25 intelligence summary regarding emergency education propaganda and trade indices.
subfiles.summary: Notes that the May 25 summary contains limited new intelligence. Highlights the Ministry of Education's forthcoming public campaign on the national emergency situation. Reports on trade balance figures, wholesale price movements, Tokyo wage levels, and government deliberations over instituting export control.
subfiles.title: Division of Far Eastern Affairs Memorandum on Tokyo Naval Attaché Bi-Weekly Summary of May 25, 1933 (Copy 1)
subfiles.to: Officers of the Division of Far Eastern Affairs

subfiles.about: Complete duplicate copy reporting on Diet legislation, the Jehol offensive, foreign diplomacy, industrial expansion, and police detentions.
subfiles.summary: Surveys Diet debates on budget items, new economic statutes, and the appointment of Kurahei Yuasa to the Imperial Household Ministry. Discusses troop preparations for operations in Jehol Province, Sino-Japanese tensions, and the rejection of a Soviet non-aggression pact. Outlines popular defense contributions, steel plant enlargements, economic distress in Tokyo, and extensive police questioning of youths and radicals.
subfiles.title: Tokyo Naval Attaché Bi-Weekly Intelligence Summary (Early 1933, Copy 2)

subfiles.about: Duplicate copy of the Far Eastern Affairs memorandum summarizing the Naval Attaché's report on emergency propaganda and economic trends.
subfiles.summary: Summarizes the Tokyo Naval Attaché's May 25 report for State Department officials. Outlines the Department of Education's plans for a national emergency campaign and evaluates recent foreign trade figures showing reduced import excess. Summarizes Tokyo wage adjustments and plans for state supervision over export trade.
subfiles.title: Division of Far Eastern Affairs Memorandum on Tokyo Naval Attaché Bi-Weekly Summary of May 25, 1933 (Copy 2)
subfiles.to: Officers of the Division of Far Eastern Affairs

subfiles.about: Highlights key political, economic, and naval items from the Tokyo Naval Attaché's May 11 summary.
subfiles.summary: Observes the growing likelihood of the Saito Cabinet remaining in power with backing from the Genro, military, and Privy Council. Outlines the War Minister's emergency declarations, the Japan International Association's reorganization, and the unbalanced Manchukuo budget estimates. Covers Soviet Far Eastern shipping expansion, Japanese naval readiness, mandated island patrols, friction over yen currency valuation, and vessel imports for scrapping.
subfiles.title: Division of Far Eastern Affairs Memorandum on Tokyo Naval Attaché Bi-Weekly Summary of May 11, 1933

subfiles.about: Covers the political status of the Saito Cabinet, hostilities in North China, Manchukuo economic schemes, and industrial mobilization.
subfiles.summary: Reviews domestic politics following the May 15 incident investigation findings and military distrust of political parties. Details combat along the Great Wall and Luan River, ambitious agricultural and mineral exploitation plans in Manchukuo, and talks regarding the sale of the Chinese Eastern Railway. Discusses Indo-Japanese tariff friction, naval aviation accidents, naval maneuvers, foreign trade balances, and agricultural debt relief.
subfiles.title: Tokyo Naval Attaché Bi-Weekly Intelligence Summary of May 11, 1933

subfiles.about: Notes the Tokyo Naval Attaché's reporting on General Ugaki's dispute with army factions and the navy's insistence on parity.
subfiles.summary: Summarizes the June 18 intelligence summary from Tokyo, focusing on political and naval matters. Reports that General Ugaki failed to reconcile his differences with the War Minister and junior officers who oppose his premiership. Relates the Naval Staff's uncompromising stance demanding naval parity with the United States and Britain at the upcoming conference.
subfiles.title: Division of Far Eastern Affairs Memorandum on Tokyo Naval Attaché Bi-Weekly Summary of June 18, 1933

subfiles.about: Surveys Cabinet political intrigues involving General Ugaki, anti-bandit campaigns in Manchukuo, C.E.R. sale talks, and university student unrest.
subfiles.summary: Analyzes friction between the Seiyukai, the War Ministry, and Governor General Ugaki over cabinet formation. Reports on extensive anti-bandit sweeps in Manchukuo, railway blockades, and scheduled Tokyo negotiations for the sale of the North Manchurian Railway. Mentions proceedings at the London Economic Conference, steel manufacturing profits, student demonstrations over the Kyoto Imperial University faculty dismissals, and rural debt adjustment schemes.
subfiles.title: Tokyo Naval Attaché Bi-Weekly Intelligence Summary of June 18, 1933

subfiles.about: Comments on an ONI translation of a Gaiko Jiho editorial interpreting recent East Asian developments as Japanese triumphs over Western influence.
subfiles.summary: Reviews an ONI translation of an editorial published in the June 15 issue of Gaiko Jiho (Diplomatic Review). Explains how the editorial presents the Tangku truce, the Soviet offer to sell the C.E.R., and Manchukuo's development as evidence of rising Japanese authority. Emphasizes the article's assertion that Japan, allied with millions of fellow Asians, is prepared to resist economic and political pressure from an Anglo-American bloc.
subfiles.title: Division of Far Eastern Affairs Memorandum on Gaiko Jiho Editorial regarding Anglo-American Oppression

subfiles.about: Translates a Japanese diplomatic review editorial advocating Asian solidarity under Japanese leadership against Western economic blocs.
subfiles.from: Gaiko Jiho (translated by E. C. Bemerth, ONI)
subfiles.summary: Asserts that Japan has entered an acute international crisis involving economic collision with the British Empire and strategic differences with the United States. Contrasts Western decline with Japan's superior spiritual civilization and argues that non-white populations look to Japan for liberation. Frames the Tangku truce as China's de facto capitulation and recognition of Manchukuo, and praises Soviet realism regarding the North Manchurian Railway while commemorating journal founder Dr. Ariga.
subfiles.title: Office of Naval Intelligence Translation: "Mission of Gaiko Jiho (Emergency and World Battle Formation Against Japan)"
subfiles.to: Director of Naval Intelligence / Division of Far Eastern Affairs

subfiles.about: Evaluates the Tokyo Naval Attaché's report of July 27, analyzing military budget estimates, the Simla trade parley, and the naval ratio dispute.
subfiles.summary: Reviews domestic Japanese budget disputes, highlighting military funding demands and Finance Minister Takahashi's opposition to increased taxation. Clarifies the role and authority of Indian delegates at the forthcoming Simla trade conference. Argues that Japan is ready to face unrestricted naval competition rather than accept a 60 percent naval ratio under existing treaties. Notes communications centralization plans and military fuel appropriations for Manchurian oil development.
subfiles.title: Division of Far Eastern Affairs Memorandum on Tokyo Naval Attaché Bi-Weekly Report of July 27, 1933

subfiles.about: Surveys political alignments, military budget requests, North China affairs, trade negotiations, and domestic security plots.
subfiles.summary: Covers the Minseito's cooperation with the Saito Cabinet and negotiations over massive military and naval budget estimates. Examines Japanese control in North China, preparations for trade talks in Simla and London, Kwantung Army force deployments, and C.E.R. purchase discussions. Discusses Soviet frontier incidents, reactions to comments by American publisher Roy Howard, nationwide air defense exercises, steel and shipping expansion, and the foiling of the Shin'eito assassination conspiracy.
subfiles.title: Tokyo Naval Attaché Bi-Weekly Intelligence Summary of July 27, 1933

subfiles.about: Highlights trade growth with Manchuria and Japanese concerns over proposed British Empire shipping restrictions.
subfiles.summary: Analyzes economic data in the Naval Attaché's August 17 report, noting a 125 percent rise in Japanese trade with Manchuria for the first half of 1933. Emphasizes Japanese anxiety regarding proposals to restrict British Empire maritime trade exclusively to British flag vessels. Observes that such measures would threaten Japanese merchant shipping lines, though the British government remains hesitant to implement full restrictions.
subfiles.title: Division of Far Eastern Affairs Memorandum on Tokyo Naval Attaché Bi-Weekly Report No. 124 of August 17, 1933

subfiles.about: Details the May 15 incident trials, the passing of Field Marshal Muto, military appointments, and industrial cartels.
subfiles.summary: Examines testimony in the May 15 court martial trials, revealing extremist conspiracies to assassinate Ambassador Grew and Charlie Chaplin in order to block naval limitation treaties. Details the death of Ambassador Field Marshal Muto in Hsinking and the appointment of General Takashi Hishikari to succeed him. Reviews C.E.R. valuation disputes, French claims to South China Sea coral islands, army disputes with Catholic mission schools, Yawata steel prices, Soviet gasoline imports, and graduate unemployment.
subfiles.title: Tokyo Naval Attaché Bi-Weekly Intelligence Summary No. 124 of August 17, 1933

subfiles.about: Analyzes the Seiyukai's policy platform, Cabinet resignation rumors, Indian cotton boycott reports, and Soviet oil distribution.
subfiles.summary: Assesses the five-point program advocated by the Seiyukai, focusing on the proposed Japan-Manchuria economic bloc and efforts to prevent a military dictatorship. Examines rumors of imminent resignations by Foreign Minister Uchida and Privy Seal Makino over soaring military budgets. Notes conflicting information on the Indian cotton boycott and discusses government non-intervention regarding the importation and marketing of Soviet petroleum products.
subfiles.title: Division of Far Eastern Affairs Memorandum on Tokyo Naval Attaché Bi-Weekly Report of September 1, 1933

subfiles.about: Forwards a copy of an ONI Bi-Weekly Intelligence Summary to the State Department.
subfiles.summary: Official Navy Department transmittal slip routing a Tokyo Bi-Weekly Intelligence Summary to the Department of State for information. Lists administrative routing checkboxes and Navy Department bureau addresses.
subfiles.title: Office of Naval Intelligence Routing Slip for Bi-Weekly Intelligence Summary

subfiles.about: Reports on the Seiyukai's policy proposals, Huang Fu's diplomacy, the Grand Naval Review, espionage investigations, and industrial output.
subfiles.summary: Details political maneuvers by the Seiyukai and other parties to avert military dictatorship, along with the assignment of diplomats to European capitals to monitor the League of Nations. Discusses the Lu-shan conference between Huang Fu and Chiang Kai-shek, the deportation of British anti-war campaigner Lord Marley, and Soviet military defense preparations in Siberia. Reviews the Grand Naval Review in Tokyo Bay, foreign warship orders, espionage allegations against foreigners, trade missions to Latin America and Africa, and industrial production data.
subfiles.title: Tokyo Naval Attaché Bi-Weekly Intelligence Summary of September 1, 1933
